entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.text: Role of a Pega Business Architect · Stakeholder interactions

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Who the Business Architect Is

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Pega Business Architect (BA)
entries.text: The liaison who bridges the client organization and the Pega delivery team, understanding business needs and Pega capabilities to produce software that exceeds what either side could build alone.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Member of BOTH teams
entries.text: On a Pega project, the BA belongs to both the Business team (process and organizational needs) and the IT team (software development and Pega capabilities), bridging the two groups.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Client vs. Customer (terminology)
entries.text: Two distinct stakeholder roles in Pega implementations: CLIENT ('organization') — the BUSINESS transforming its workflows with Pega · CUSTOMER — that business's END CUSTOMER (the person using the final application)

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: The Four Core Responsibilities (A-P-A-E)

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Analysis
entries.text: Gather a complete picture of problems before configuring a solution: Understand critical stages · Identify bottlenecks and workarounds · Diagnose root causes · Find functionality common across processes

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Process Design
entries.text: Optimize the workflow using Pega GenAI Blueprint: Remove unnecessary steps · Re-sequence stages · Automate repetitive activities · Intelligently allocate work · Consolidate data for users

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Alignment
entries.text: Collaborate with Business and IT to design, build, and test the solution using Blueprint and App Studio, ensuring both sides understand requirements and the proposed workflow improvements.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Education
entries.text: Continuously teach Business stakeholders the value of Pega's out-of-the-box features, helping them focus on outcomes rather than current methods and become advocates for the new process.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Partnership in Action (worked example)

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Common Responsibilities Across All Projects

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Facilitating requirement-gathering meetings
entries.text: Organize and facilitate focused meetings with stakeholders and SMEs to gather and document business processes and requirements, guiding stakeholder understanding by translating how OOTB Pega features meet business requirements.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Documenting requirements as user stories
entries.text: Document business requirements as user stories using Blueprint, App Studio's Agile workbench, and other Scrum tools. Pega developers (System Architects) use those user stories to configure the application to make the best use of Pega's strengths.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Demonstrating OOTB functionality
entries.text: Use Blueprint to quickly redesign a workflow based on OOTB features and case-management best practices (building stakeholder alignment), and use App Studio to demonstrate how additional Pega features address requirements.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Promoting Pega best practices
entries.text: Across the project landscape — organizational structure, user-story and backlog creation, governance, and testing — the BA follows and instructs on Pega's proven best practices throughout design and delivery.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Core Delivery Team Stakeholders

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Product Owner (PO)
entries.text: A client Business-team representative primarily responsible for managing project SCOPE and PRIORITIZING requirements throughout development. The BA runs user-story review meetings with the PO to finalize acceptance criteria and prioritize the backlog so desired features land in the timeline.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Project Delivery Lead (PDL)
entries.text: The project manager who leads the Pega delivery team, maintains governance, and liaises with client leadership on timeline, budget, and scope — the BA works with the PDL on governance decisions.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Scrum Master
entries.text: Promotes and supports Scrum; organizes the team, facilitates ceremonies (Sprint Planning, Sizing, Backlog Refinement, Retrospective), and is accountable for team success and removing blockers.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: System Architects (SA / SSA / LSA)
entries.text: The Pega developers (SA, SSA, LSA) who configure the application. The LSA imports the Blueprint and configures requirements from user stories; BAs translate technical information for stakeholders.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Quality Analysts (QAs)
entries.text: Ensure functionality meets documented requirements. QAs build test scripts from user stories, participate in sizing, and flag defects. The BA helps decide if a flagged item is a defect or a new requirement.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Business-Side and Specialist Stakeholders

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Subject Matter Experts (SMEs)
entries.text: Client representatives with first-hand knowledge of the business process steps. BAs collaborate with SMEs in an operational walkthrough to observe the as-is process and capture all work, in and out of the system.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Business Analysts
entries.text: Client representatives primarily responsible for documenting the current 'as-is' process, data requirements, and business requirements. The BA reviews this documentation to identify redundancies and bottlenecks, recommend automations, determine resource needs, and define data/interface details.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: UX Designers
entries.text: Ensure the design meets end-user needs, complies with accessibility standards, and delivers a consistent experience across all delivery Channels. The BA collaborates to align the UI with UX requirements, maximize OOTB features, and meet business objectives.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Solutions Consultant
entries.text: Works with the client during the initial sales phase, often designing the Blueprint with stakeholders, then transitions the Blueprint to the delivery BAs and System Architects before the project starts.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Parallel Development: Workspaces & Branches

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Workspace
entries.text: A secure, private space for one operator to build and manage features in one application independently. Changes stay private until shared to a Branch, preventing rule conflicts during parallel development.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Branch
entries.text: A Ruleset container for rapidly changing records, letting teams develop features in isolation. One Branch per feature is the standard strategy; changes are only shared once stable, conflict-free, and approved.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Blueprint import → Branch (except Access Roles)
entries.text: When importing a Blueprint into Pega Platform, all assets are created in a Branch except Access Roles, which are handled separately outside the Branch.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Key Skills and Knowledge

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Analytical & problem-solving skills
entries.text: Break down complex business processes and identify opportunities for improvement and simplification.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Process design knowledge
entries.text: Process design skills and knowledge of business process design to innovate new processes and ways of working that achieve the outcome.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Systems design, Pega technology & Blueprint knowledge
entries.text: Understand Pega's architecture, out-of-the-box features, and Blueprint so business requirements and end-user needs can be mapped to the right Pega capabilities and solutions.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Active listening, communication & facilitation
entries.text: Create a common language and shared understanding of both the business need and Pega's capabilities across the project team and stakeholders.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.title: Knowledge of business change
entries.text: Help the Business team embrace the new Pega solution and become advocates for it within their organization.

entries.title: Low-code defined
entries.text: Low-code application development · Studios · App Studio · Dev Studio · Integrating with external applications

entries.title: Low-code development
entries.text: Products and cloud services that use visual, declarative techniques instead of programming. As you manipulate the visual model, tools generate the underlying code — Pega has done this for 30 years.

entries.title: Value of low-code
entries.text: Low-code bridges business stakeholders and skilled developers with a common visual language, enabling teams to deliver faster, collaborate better, and focus on business logic rather than code.

entries.title: Omnichannel reach
entries.text: The same Pega application can serve as a web page, mobile app, or chatbot; data can arrive via email or a robot. Organizations unify all channels without maintaining disparate code lines.

entries.title: Low-code AND professional developers
entries.text: Visual, end-to-end tools make everyone more productive. Citizen developers create application code; experienced developers extend robust applications more rapidly, hide implementation, and build patterns once to reuse many times across the ecosystem.

entries.title: App Studio
entries.text: A low-code authoring space providing CORE features: Case design, data management, and user experience (UI). Users: citizen developers plus technical staff — application developers, front-end developers, data engineers, business analysts, and System Architects. The place to get applications operating quickly.

entries.title: Dev Studio
entries.text: A low-code authoring space with ADVANCED features. Technical users: full-stack developers, System Architects, and database/security administrators. Used for complex Rule configuration, security/access control, reuse management, and performance.

entries.title: Prediction Studio
entries.text: An ANALYTICS space for data scientists and business decision-makers, providing features to build machine-learning models for adaptive, predictive, and text analytics. Access requires pxPredictionStudio among the Portals on the user's access group.

entries.title: Admin Studio
entries.text: A software ADMINISTRATION space managed by IT for system administration — runtime information and configuration options for monitoring and debugging system resources.

entries.title: Three areas of every studio
entries.text: Every studio has three regions: A Header (menus and the upper-left studio-switcher) · A Navigation pane (explorers like Case Type and Data) · An Authoring space where you configure behavior

entries.title: Support for agile development
entries.text: App Studio supports agile best practices and REAL-TIME UI design while processing work. A team testing an online-shopping UI can add fields and change controls (e.g., drop-downs) live — ideal for stakeholder reviews where feedback is implemented in real time.

entries.title: Application profile
entries.text: Captures and presents user stories, bugs, and feedback items to support agile best practices and collaboration across technical and business members. Provides traceability from objectives to development tasks to implementation.

entries.title: Rules
entries.text: Instructions that govern application behavior (like the rules of chess govern the pieces). As you build visually, Pega auto-generates Rules in the background using the SAME names you choose — which is why business-friendly names matter.

entries.title: Layers & Rulesets
entries.text: Rules are organized into reusable Layers; each Layer is a unique application built on one or more others. Rulesets store, manage, and identify Rules that can be shared and reused as a whole unit.

entries.title: Application Layers Widget & OOTB architectures
entries.text: The App Studio overview's Application Layers Widget visualizes your Rulesets and identifies the application type. Two OOTB architectures: Constellation architecture (Constellation Ruleset, new View-based UI) and Traditional UI architecture (Theme Cosmos Ruleset, Section-based UI).

entries.title: Dev Studio: Co-development, Reuse, and Naming
Domain vs. Implementation experts
entries.text: Two groups defined by Pega for co-development: DOMAIN experts (Business Analysts, Citizen Developers, front-end developers) — provide process/user insight; primarily work in App Studio · IMPLEMENTATION experts (System Architects, full-stack/DB/security admins) — handle complex configuration; primarily work in Dev Studio

entries.title: Co-development
entries.text: Business and IT work together: a Business Analyst designs Views in App Studio while a System Architect adds advanced logic in Dev Studio, combining domain insight with implementation expertise.

entries.title: Promote reuse by extending Rule scope
entries.text: In Dev Studio, developers access all layers and extend a rule's scope from one Case Type to an application, division, or whole organization, creating a reusable library that cuts future development time.

entries.title: Advanced SLA options in Dev Studio
entries.text: Beyond App Studio's basic goal/deadline, Dev Studio exposes: Initialization behavior (custom initial urgency, delayed timer start) · Variable interval length (programmatic durations per Case) · Account-for-business-days (exclude holidays/weekends) · Additional escalation actions (reassign a task or resolve a Case)

entries.title: Integration connectors
entries.text: Pega supports many integration standards and protocols so you focus on business requirements. A standard API connector exchanges data in real time when both systems support a common protocol.

entries.title: Robotic Process Automation (RPA)
entries.text: Used when no other integration is feasible — typically legacy systems with no usable API. A robot interacts with the system's UI to perform the same steps a person would, but far faster.

entries.title: Attended RPA
entries.text: Automation that works ALONGSIDE a human in the process, in real time. Example: a CSR triggers a robot mid-call to update an address by driving the legacy system's UI while the customer waits.

entries.title: Unattended RPA
entries.text: The request is placed in a QUEUE for later background processing. Advantages: optimizes system resources, reduces peak loads, and lets the CSR keep serving the customer instead of waiting for the update to finish.

entries.title: Pega Robot Manager
entries.text: A control-tower application that lets you monitor and schedule RPA robots and provides performance analytics for all robots.

entries.title: Pega Center-out architecture
entries.text: Pega's Center-out business architecture · Accessibility in Center-out Development

entries.title: Top-down approach
entries.text: Designs applications around the PRESENTATION layer's delivery Channels (web, mobile, digital messaging, voice-AI). Its most significant disadvantage: the same business logic must be implemented MULTIPLE TIMES to deliver a consistent experience across the different Channels.

entries.title: Bottom-up approach
entries.text: Designs applications around the DATA access layer first. The risk: each system maintains its own data view, creating integration complexity and inconsistency across channels.

entries.title: Center-out business architecture
entries.text: Puts BUSINESS LOGIC at the center of application design. Customer-facing channels and back-end data sources connect to this central layer, so logic is defined once and shared across all touchpoints.

entries.title: Presentation layer (connects UP)
entries.text: The business logic is connected up into the presentation layer so delivery Channels dynamically RESPOND to changes in the central business logic — no recoding per channel.

entries.title: Application & business logic layer (the hub)
entries.text: The central hub containing all the business logic needed to achieve the desired strategic outcome for the organization.

entries.title: Data access layer (connects DOWN)
entries.text: Connections down to data are insulated from the business logic, so changes in systems of record — for example, moving from on-premise to Cloud storage — do NOT require changes in the application's business logic.

entries.title: 1. Manage intelligence centrally
entries.text: Center-out principle 1 — start with the business logic: Business outcomes guided by real-time customer information · Rules consistently enforced across all channels · Everyone uses the SAME intelligence (single source of truth)

entries.title: 2. Focus on outcomes, align your process
entries.text: Get the work done using Case Management and a MICROJOURNEY approach — implementing a part of the customer journey that is tied to a specific outcome.

entries.title: 3. Connect experiences up to your Channels
entries.text: Provide a consistent user experience by keeping front-end and back-end logic coordinated; changes are reflected dynamically without recoding.

entries.title: 4. Connect down to your data, keep logic nimble
entries.text: Access data without adding complexity — quickly and easily define the data needed and access it in running applications without worrying about how or where the data is stored or accessed.

entries.title: 5. Manage variations to be scale-ready
entries.text: Start small and fast, then scale big and broad and stay future-proof by adapting to different customer types, lines of business, and geographies using Pega's SITUATIONAL LAYER CAKE.

entries.title: Efficiency
entries.text: Developers define business rules ONCE in a central location, eliminating duplication and reducing inconsistencies across channels and applications.

entries.title: Agility
entries.text: When business requirements change, you update the CENTRAL logic and the system applies those changes across all channel interfaces — making applications more responsive to evolving needs.

entries.title: Governance
entries.text: Centralized business rules simplify auditing, monitoring, and policy enforcement consistently across all interfaces and channels from one authoritative location.

entries.title: Scalability
entries.text: As the organization adds new channel interfaces or customer touchpoints, you REUSE existing business logic to maintain consistency.

entries.title: Model-driven UI
entries.text: An approach in which the underlying data models and business rules GENERATE the user interface. In Center-out, these models reside at the core and the system dynamically generates the UI from them.

entries.title: Patterns
entries.text: Reusable UI templates that implement a model-driven approach: define the Data Model and business rules once, then the UI assembles the correct layout automatically.

entries.title: Separation of logic and presentation
entries.text: A key advantage of patterns: when business rules change, the UI ADAPTS AUTOMATICALLY without manual updates. Pattern-based UIs also support responsive design across devices and channels.

entries.title: Centralized accessibility
entries.text: Shared UI patterns can distribute accessibility improvements across the experiences that use them, reducing repeated implementation work. Custom content, configuration, integrations, and user interactions still need application-specific evaluation.

entries.title: Standards supported
entries.text: The referenced curriculum describes support for WCAG 2.1 and Section 508 through core components. Support for a standard is not proof that a particular application conforms; assess the applicable requirements and the actual experience.

entries.title: Evolving standards
entries.text: Update shared components to distribute relevant fixes to consuming applications. Confirm that each application adopts the changes, then evaluate its content and interactions against the applicable requirements.

entries.title: Modular architecture and enterprise reuse
entries.text: Modular reuse architecture · Studio interoperability and the Reuse Library

entries.title: Modular enterprise reuse
entries.text: A software development approach that uses standardized, reusable components to build applications. Instead of starting from scratch, developers ASSEMBLE pre-built, tested modules to speed up development and maintain consistency across the enterprise.

entries.title: Benefits across the lifecycle
entries.text: Reusing shared modules helps at every project phase: Design: reduces planning time with ready-made components · Development: speeds builds and minimizes coding · Testing: limits defects/scope via pre-tested modules · Deployment: simplifies implementation with standardized components · Maintenance: enables automatic updates across all applications using shared modules

entries.title: The Five Guiding Principles of Reuse
Interoperable
entries.text: Use consistent building blocks across applications AND authoring environments (App Studio and Dev Studio).

entries.title: Updateable
entries.text: Individual components can be updated independently without disrupting the entire application or requiring changes to every consuming module.

entries.title: Configurable
entries.text: Behavior can be adjusted through configuration settings without rewriting the underlying business logic, enabling business-led customization.

entries.title: Modular
entries.text: Applications are assembled from encapsulated, self-contained components rather than built as large monolithic layers that are difficult to maintain or update.

entries.title: Governed
entries.text: Establish governance (for example, a Pega Center of Excellence) to manage, evolve, and ensure the quality of reusable assets.

entries.title: Situational Layer Cake
entries.text: A patented Pega architecture that balances two competing forces: REUSE (economies of scale and consistency) and VARIATION (different products, regions, regulatory needs). It avoids both 'spaghetti' single-app if-then-else and the sprawl of 50–100 near-identical apps.

entries.title: Enterprise Layer
entries.text: Core Pega Platform features and enterprise-wide reusable assets (e.g., a company-wide authentication module used across all applications).

entries.title: Division Layer
entries.text: Reusable components specific to a division (e.g., a claims-processing flow tailored for the insurance division but reused across its applications).

entries.title: Application Layer
entries.text: Application-specific implementations that leverage lower-layer assets (e.g., a customer-service app that uses shared authentication and claims components but adds its own workflows).

entries.title: Implementation Layer
entries.text: Customizations for specific deployment scenarios WITHOUT altering the base application (e.g., localizing the customer-service app for a region by adjusting language and regulatory rules).

entries.title: App Studio role
entries.text: A simplified, collaborative, inclusive authoring experience that lets a wide range of low-code practitioners understand, interpret, and author processes/applications. It hides complexity and raises Case Type literacy so stakeholders express requirements and feedback better.

entries.title: Dev Studio role
entries.text: Robust low-code environment for experienced architects to configure integrations, complex decisions, security, and advanced features beyond App Studio's scope.

entries.title: Relevant records
entries.text: Rules marked as relevant records become available for assembly in App Studio, enabling Studio interoperability and exposing reusable assets to business-level authors.

entries.title: Auto-marked in App Studio
entries.text: When you create Fields, Views, Processes, and user actions in App Studio, Pega automatically marks them as relevant records.

entries.title: Reuse Library
entries.text: A centralized repository in App Studio that contains all reusable assets in the enterprise, helping developers of all skill levels discover, understand, and use reusable components. Combined with strong governance, it accelerates development, improves quality, and boosts agility.

entries.title: Creating a Rule
entries.text: Rules and Rule Types · Rulesets · Rule creation · Classes and class hierarchy · Rule reuse through inheritance

entries.title: Rule
entries.text: The basic building block of a Pega application. Each Rule is an instance of a Rule Type (e.g., a Flow Rule models a Process). Rules define application behavior without custom coding.

entries.title: Rule Type
entries.text: A template for creating a Rule that models a specific behavior — for example, a Flow Rule models a Process, while other Rule Types model UI, automated Decisions, and more.

entries.title: Automated Rule creation in App Studio
entries.text: App Studio auto-creates Rules as you design: Adding Processes creates Flow Rules · Defining Steps creates Flow Action Rules · Configuring Views creates Section/Harness Rules

entries.title: Versioning
entries.text: Creating a new version of a Rule whenever Case behavior must change. Pega keeps a full change history, enabling rollback of a specific Rule without affecting others.

entries.title: Delegation
entries.text: Exposing a specific Rule to business users so they can update Case behavior as conditions change, without filing an IT change request or touching other rules.

entries.title: Reuse
entries.text: Developers reuse Rules whenever an application needs existing behavior, instead of reconfiguring it every time (e.g., reuse one policyholder-info UI form across auto, property, and marine claims).

entries.title: Parametrization
entries.text: To increase reusability, use parameters to drive a Rule's logic based on a passed value instead of hard-coded data — reducing code duplication and the time to implement Rule specializations.

entries.title: Ruleset
entries.text: A group that identifies, stores, and manages the Rules defining an application or a significant portion of it. Rulesets enable versioning, access control, and portability.

entries.title: Ruleset version
entries.text: An instance of a Ruleset collecting individual Rules. To update contents you create a NEW version (unlocked), add/change Rules, then lock it when complete.

entries.title: Ruleset stack
entries.text: The sequence of Rulesets in an application determining the ORDER Pega searches to find a Rule at run time. The most-specific Ruleset is searched first.

entries.title: Two paths to a Rule
entries.text: In App Studio, Rules are created FOR you as you build the Case Life Cycle, Views, and data. In Dev Studio, you can directly create and manage how a Rule is created and reused to maintain Rule integrity and reusability.

entries.title: Specialization by copy (Save As)
entries.text: You can copy an existing Rule into a different class or Ruleset to specialize its behavior, rather than building from scratch — preserving the original while creating a variant.

entries.title: Class
entries.text: A grouping of Rules according to their capacity for reuse: Work class (process Cases) · Integration class (connect to systems) · Data class (describe data types)

entries.title: Parent and child classes
entries.text: A class can contain other classes. A parent class contains another class; a child class is contained by another. A child class can reuse/inherit any Rules defined for its parent class.

entries.title: Class hierarchy
entries.text: Classes are layered from most-specific to least-specific. Pega starts at the most-specific class and expands the search upward until a matching Rule is found.

entries.title: Pattern inheritance
entries.text: Automatic inheritance using the existing class-name prefix structure to determine parent classes — no explicit configuration required. Promotes reuse by business suitability.

entries.title: Directed inheritance
entries.text: Inheritance where the parent class is EXPLICITLY specified on the class form. It lets an application class inherit from standard Pega classes outside the naming hierarchy.

entries.title: Resolution order & @baseclass
entries.text: Pega alternates pattern and directed searches up the class hierarchy. If no Rule is found by @baseclass, Pega returns a Rule-not-found error.

entries.title: Pega GenAI in Pega Platform
entries.text: Generative AI in Pega · Generating a Case Type using Pega GenAI Autopilot · Generating Case Data using Pega GenAI Autopilot · Generating Personas using Pega GenAI Autopilot

entries.title: Pega GenAI
entries.text: A suite of generative AI-powered features integrated across Pega Platform, available beginning with Pega Infinity '23. It helps developers, learners, and users build applications, enhance learning, improve operational efficiency, and stay aligned with best practices.

entries.title: Pega Blueprint
entries.text: A SaaS tool that turns application ideas into reusable, collaborative production apps (often within ~90 days). After you describe goals, Blueprint instantly suggests an optimal application design including Case Types, Live Data, and Personas.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Autopilot
entries.text: Pairs App Studio accelerators for workflows and data with a conversational assistant trained on Pega documentation and developer training, enabling developers to build applications about twice as fast. Autopilot covers all generative AI features available at DESIGN time.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Connect
entries.text: Lets you develop custom Pega GenAI-powered capabilities using the Pega GenAI gateway; an add-on compatible with Pega Platform, Customer Service, or Sales Automation.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Coach
entries.text: Provides expert advice and feedback on END-USER tasks at application RUNTIME — ideal for task-specific guidance relevant to a Pega Case.

entries.title: Generative AI — Run-Time Tools and Custom AI
Pega GenAI Agent and Tool Rules
entries.text: Automate Case processing and provide conversational support for run-time users. Agents perform automated actions and offer run-time guidance to accelerate Case processing; Tool Rules add governance, security, and compliance.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Knowledge Buddy
entries.text: Gives employees, agents, and sellers instant answers and real-time guidance via a conversation interface, combining Pega GenAI with the organization's own procedural documents and knowledge bases.

entries.title: Search Assistant & OpenAI search
entries.text: Search Assistant integrates with Pega Community search (powered by Knowledge Buddy) to link relevant materials. OpenAI search on the Pega Documentation site answers questions when you add a question mark to the end of a search query.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Autopilot at Design Time
What Autopilot accelerates
entries.text: Autopilot delivers real-time, context-aware guidance and task prioritization during development. For a loan app, it suggests application components including Case Types, fields in the Data Model, and Personas — and developers can review and modify any recommendation before generating it.

entries.title: The Autopilot workflow
entries.text: When you create a Case Type, Autopilot suggests names, a workflow, data objects, and Personas — accelerating design-time setup with AI-generated proposals the architect reviews and accepts.

entries.title: Human-in-the-loop responsibility
entries.text: Pega is NOT responsible for the content of Autopilot suggestions — always review AI-powered recommendations before accepting them.

entries.title: Blueprint as a SaaS design tool
entries.text: A standalone SaaS tool that designs new applications and Case Types independently of Pega Platform, requiring no Pega login for collaboration. It augments App Studio rather than replacing it.

entries.title: What Blueprint proposes
entries.text: From a business-terms description, Blueprint proposes Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas, plus best-practice application templates, enabling quick design edits to fit requirements.

entries.title: Connect Generative AI automation Step
entries.text: A Step (available since Pega Infinity '24) that calls a configured GenAI Connect Rule from App Studio to send a prompt to an LLM and receive a response in one of three structures.

entries.title: Three response structures
entries.text: GenAI response types and their Data Model mapping: Structured-Single: one object mapped to a Data Model field · Structured-List: multiple objects mapped to a page list · Unstructured: raw text mapped to a Text (paragraph) field

entries.title: Target field requirement
entries.text: You must identify a target field to write the response into, and add that target field to the application UI so the response can be displayed to the user.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Agent and Tool Rules
Agents
entries.text: Configurable AI assistants that automate Case processing and provide run-time guidance. Governed by Tool Rules, they can run automations, start Cases, call other agents, and converse with users.

entries.title: Guardrails via Tool Rules
entries.text: Detailed descriptions and guardrails ensure the agent responds precisely; at run time users converse with agents in natural-language chat. Agents can also process and extract data from uploaded documents, saving manual analysis time.
