entries.text: Lesson 02 - Attributes (video)

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestSheets and Attributes

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestSheet
entries.text: The highest-level object in the TestCase Design section. A TestSheet organizes the test data and logical test structure for one Requirement — as a rule of thumb, one TestSheet is created per Requirement, and the TestCases built from it will cover that Requirement.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Attribute
entries.text: A characteristic or business object involved in the behavior being tested — for example, a credit-card drop-down on a checkout form. Attributes describe *what varies*; the specific values an Attribute can take (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) are added later as Instances (Lesson 3).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Structuring Attributes
entries.text: Like Requirements, Attributes can be layered — every Attribute may have sub-Attributes, depending on how much detail the TestSheet needs.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: AttrType: Logical vs Physical

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: AttrType is system-determined, not user-set
entries.text: Every Attribute has an AttrType property with value 'Logical' or 'Physical'. This isn't something you choose from a dropdown — Tosca sets it automatically based on structure: an Attribute with sub-Attributes underneath it is Logical; an Attribute with none is Physical.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The four core Attributes

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Recommended structure
entries.text: Tricentis recommends starting every TestSheet with four top-level logical Attributes, so that any reader can immediately see the role each block of data plays.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: BusinessRelevant property

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Three possible values
entries.text: BusinessRelevant is set by the user (unlike AttrType) and controls whether an Attribute's data affects TestCase combinations.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Building it in Tosca

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 3 - Instances
entries.text: Lesson 03 - Instances (video)

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: What is an Instance

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Instance
entries.text: A concrete variation/value of an Attribute — for example, if 'Credit Card Type' is the Attribute, then Visa, Mastercard, and Amex are its Instances. Instances are added via the Ribbon, 'Add Instance' in the Mini-Toolbar, or the shortcut Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Character: Valid, Invalid, StraightThrough

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Valid (default)
entries.text: A white Instance icon with an 'I', outlined in red. Applying a Valid Instance should NOT produce an error in the process.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Invalid
entries.text: Same icon style but with an 'X' instead of an 'I'. Applying an Invalid Instance SHOULD produce an error or error message — this does not mean the TestCase fails; a correctly-appearing error message is a pass for an Invalid TestCase. Example: testing login with an invalid password should verify the user is NOT logged in and the correct error message appears.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: StraightThrough
entries.text: A special category of Instance chosen according to specific criteria: it should be high-risk if it failed, easy to implement, and have the fewest dependencies (so it can combine with as many Instances from other Attributes as possible). Often called the 'happy path' and typically included in the smoke test.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Position: Inner vs Boundary

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Boundary Value
entries.text: A value at the edge of a valid range. If an accepted age range is 1-99, the values immediately around each edge (0, 1, 99, 100) are Boundary Values — they carry a high probability of error because off-by-one logic mistakes (e.g. '>1' coded instead of '>=1') tend to surface exactly there.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why Boundaries are usually one-time tests
entries.text: As long as the range doesn't change between releases, a Boundary error is a one-time class of bug — so Boundary Values are typically used in one-time tests rather than every regression run.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Inner Value (default)
entries.text: Any value in the range that isn't immediately around a boundary — e.g. 2 through 98 in the age example. These don't need to be tested one by one; instead, group them into a single representative Instance called an Equivalence Class (e.g. one Instance covering 2-98, optionally randomized at execution time using a Tosca RND expression). Equivalence Classes are a good fit for regression tests.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 4 - Combinatorial Methods
entries.text: Lesson 04 - Combinatorial Methods (video)

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The four combinatorial methods

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: All Combinations
entries.text: Every possible combination of Instance values across the combined Attributes is generated. This produces the highest number of TestCases — for 3 Attributes with 3 Instances each, that's 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 combinations. Thorough, but the TestCase count (and execution time) grows very fast as Attributes/Instances are added.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Orthogonal
entries.text: Produces the lowest possible number of combinations. The only requirement is that every Instance value is used at least once. The number of resulting combinations equals the highest Instance count among the combined Attributes — for 3 Attributes with 3 Instances each, that's just 3 combinations. If Attributes have unequal Instance counts, values from the Attribute(s) with fewer Instances repeat until the Attribute with the most Instances is exhausted.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Pairwise
entries.text: Combines every possible pair of values between two Attributes. Not a primary focus of this course.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Linear Expansion (Tricentis-recommended)
entries.text: Starts from a StraightThrough baseline — the first TestCase uses the StraightThrough Instance from every combined Attribute (essentially the smoke test). Every subsequent combination swaps out exactly one StraightThrough Instance for a single non-StraightThrough Instance. This continues until every non-StraightThrough Instance has appeared at least once. Each generated TestCase therefore differs from the baseline in only one place, giving it a clear, isolated test focus.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Choosing a method

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: It depends on the project
entries.text: The right method depends on the Requirement's specification level, regulatory/legal constraints, and project context. Some industries mandate All Combinations for specific high-risk Requirements. Where there's no such constraint, Tricentis recommends Linear Expansion as the default because of its balance between coverage and clarity of test focus.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Building combinations manually in Tosca

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Instances as combination columns
entries.text: Once generated, combinations appear as Instance columns on the level where they were built — at the TestSheet level, or at an individual Attribute's level. Each combined Instance column represents one TestCase-to-be. Under Linear Expansion, the first generated column is the all-StraightThrough baseline; each subsequent column swaps in one non-StraightThrough value.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Combining at Attribute level vs TestSheet level
entries.text: Combinations don't have to be built only at the top TestSheet level — they can also be built lower, on an individual Attribute (e.g. combining just the sub-Attributes under 'Credit Card'). Once an Attribute-level combination exists, the TestSheet level only needs to reference the Instance name from that Attribute, and its values auto-populate. Attribute-level combinations show highlighted in light yellow at the TestSheet level, so you can see at a glance that a block of data was pre-combined lower down.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Keeping a TestSheet manageable

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Arrange Instances
entries.text: Right-click the TestSheet, or use 'Optimize Instances' → 'Arrange Instances' in the Ribbon, to sort Instance columns into a consistent order: StraightThrough first, then Valid Inner, then Invalid, then Boundary, then Invalid Boundary.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Merge Instance Duplicates
entries.text: Available in the Ribbon and the context menu — finds Instance columns that are identical and removes all but one, keeping the TestSheet lean.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 5 - TestCase Specifications
entries.text: Lesson 05 - TestCase Specifications (video)

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: From combinations to physical values

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why more filling-in is needed
entries.text: The previous lesson combined the business-relevant Process data needed to determine how many TestCases exist. Now the TestSheet still needs its non-business-relevant and Result Attributes populated (typically Administration and Verification) — these are the actual values that will later be linked to TestStepValues when the physical TestCase Template is built in the blue TestCase section.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Fill Empty Values

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Fill Empty Values → Specific
entries.text: Right-click an Attribute and choose 'Fill Empty Values' → 'Specific' to populate every empty cell in that Attribute's row with one chosen value in a single action — for example, setting 'Test Designer' to the same name across every TestCase column at once. If Instances already exist for that Attribute, simply pick the desired Instance from the dropdown and every empty cell is populated.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Filtering before filling

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: When one value per row isn't enough
entries.text: Sometimes different TestCases in the same row need different values — e.g. the StraightThrough should be tagged as a smoke test, Inner Valid Instances as regression tests, and Boundaries as one-time tests. Filling the whole row at once won't work here; filtering first does.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Using the Filter Column
entries.text: Make the Filter Column visible via the Column Chooser. On the level you want to filter (e.g. the TestSheet level, to filter its Instances), a dropdown lets you deselect 'ALL' and choose specific Instances, or filter by Character/Position (Inner, Valid, Boundary, etc). With the filter active, only the matching columns are visible/editable, so you can enter values just for that subset.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Value Attributes

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: What a Value Attribute is
entries.text: A Value Attribute is simply an Attribute with no Instances and no sub-Attributes defined. Instead of adding Instances and selecting them, you type the actual value directly into the cell on the TestSheet — for example, typing a real email address rather than creating an 'Email' Attribute with Instance values.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The critical rule: enter at the lowest combined level
entries.text: A Value Attribute's data must be entered at the lowest level on which its related Values were already combined — not necessarily the TestSheet level. For example, if an email address is tied to the 'Registered' Instance of a 'Type of User' Attribute, the email must be typed in at the 'Type of User' level. Entering it at the TestSheet level instead makes Tosca think you're defining a brand-new, different 'type of user' variation — which breaks the existing combinations rather than attaching data to the one that already exists.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Hands-on

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 6 - Classes
entries.text: Lesson 06 - Classes (video)

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: What a Class is

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Class
entries.text: A reusable Tosca object — conceptually similar to a Library in the TestCase section — that lets you define an Attribute structure (with its Instances and combinations) once and reuse it across many TestSheets via a Class Reference. A typical candidate is data that shows up repeatedly, like a Customer Attribute structure used by every TestSheet that touches customer data.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why it matters
entries.text: Reuse saves setup time, and because a Class Reference stays linked to its source Class, updating the Class once propagates that change to every TestSheet referencing it — centralizing maintenance instead of repeating it in every TestSheet.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Four ways to create a Class

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Dragging an Attribute WITHOUT top-level combinations
entries.text: If the Attribute structure you drag doesn't already have Instances/combinations at its top level, Tosca asks you to choose: 'Create Class from Attribute' copies the structure AND auto-generates Instance combinations based on the combinations that already existed in the source TestSheet. 'Create Structure from Attribute' copies only the Attribute/Instance structure, with no combinations.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Working with Class References

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Editing a Class
entries.text: Once created, a Class can be modified exactly like a TestSheet — add or remove Attributes, create or delete Instances, adjust combinations, and set Character/Position on its Instances.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Resolve Class Reference
entries.text: As with Libraries, if you want to change or remove a Class without affecting the values currently shown in a particular reference, select 'Resolve Class Reference' on that reference first. This breaks the live link, letting that instance of the data be modified or the Class removed independently.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Unused Instances vs irrelevant Attributes
entries.text: Not every Instance in a Class needs to be used in every TestSheet that references it — Instances not selected in a given Class Reference's combinations are shown bolded in the TestSheet. Separately, whole Attributes inside a Class Reference can be marked irrelevant for a specific TestSheet using the 'Relevant' column (add it via the Column Chooser): unchecking the box for an Attribute grays it out. Press F11 to toggle hiding/revealing these irrelevant Attributes.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Hands-on

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 7 - Link to Requirements
entries.text: Lesson 07 - Link to Requirements (video)

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why link TestCase Design back to Requirements

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Purpose
entries.text: Linking gives an early-stage overview of how much of the planned test design work maps onto the defined Requirements — how much of the project has actually been thought through and structured, before a single physical TestCase is built.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: How to link

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Drag and drop
entries.text: Drag Instances from the TestSheet onto their matching Requirement. If every Instance on the TestSheet belongs to that Requirement, the whole TestSheet can be dragged at once. If only some Instances are in scope right now — for example, only the ones planned for the current sprint — select and drag just those individual Instances instead.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestCase-Substitute link
entries.text: The result of linking Instances to a Requirement before any physical TestCase exists. It's a placeholder link showing how many TestCases will eventually need to be built in the TestCase section to cover that Requirement.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestCase link
entries.text: Once the physical TestCases are actually built (in the blue TestCase section) and linked to the same Requirements, the earlier TestCase-Substitute links become full TestCase links — reflecting real, executable TestCases instead of a planning placeholder.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestSheet-to-Requirement ratio

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Rule of thumb: one TestSheet per Requirement
entries.text: A TestSheet should contain all the TestCases needed to cover its Requirement. In sprint-based projects this can differ slightly — one TestSheet might accumulate TestCases created across multiple sprints for the same Requirement, rather than being rebuilt each sprint.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Building the project dashboard

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: ExecutionLists link to RequirementSets, not individual Requirements
entries.text: When ExecutionLists are created, they are linked to the whole RequirementSet rather than to a single Requirement. This rolls up progress across the entire set: which TestCases have been defined, which Requirements are actively being worked on, how far along the project is, and — once executions have actually run — which passed and which failed.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Hands-on

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 8 - Integration of New Attributes
entries.text: Lesson 08 - Integration of New Attributes (video)

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why this comes up

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The scenario
entries.text: Applications evolve — new features get added to the system under test after a TestSheet already exists. When a new feature affects existing test data, the TestSheet needs a new Attribute (and its Instances) integrated into the structure that's already in place, without starting over.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Where to add it
entries.text: Create the new Attribute wherever it logically fits in the existing structure — it can be added right alongside Attributes that already have combinations, even if that means the existing combination set now needs to account for it.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Updating combinations at every level

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The core rule
entries.text: After adding the new Attribute and its Instances, combinations must be completed at every level, from the lowest Attribute up to the TestSheet. Depending on the case, this can mean two different things.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Worked example: adding a Shipping Method

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The change
entries.text: A WebShop adds a new 'Shipping Method' choice at checkout, affecting shipping cost. This requires a new 'Shipping Method' Attribute with Instances for each option: Ground Shipping (the default/StraightThrough — 'Standard'), Next Day Air, Second Day Air, and an 'N/A' Instance for cases where shipping doesn't apply (e.g. In-Store Pickup, No Shipping).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Updating the lower (Checkout) level
entries.text: Existing Checkout-level Instances need the new Attribute's value filled in: the existing 'Standard'/StraightThrough Instance gets 'Ground', and the existing In-Store Pickup / No Shipping Instances get 'N/A'. Because Next Day Air and Second Day Air don't correspond to any existing Checkout Instance, two brand-new Checkout-level Instances are created for them — populated with StraightThrough values everywhere except the new Shipping Method field, which takes the respective new value.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Updating the TestSheet level
entries.text: The existing 9 TestSheet-level Instances each need the correct Checkout Instance selected for their row. Then, matching the two new Checkout-level Instances, two new TestSheet-level Instances are added — all StraightThrough values, except the Checkout Attribute, where each selects its corresponding new Checkout Instance (Next Day Air / Second Day Air).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Don't forget: re-link to Requirements

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 9 - Best Practices
entries.text: Lesson 09 - Best Practices (video)

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Design for reuse

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Spot reuse early
entries.text: When creating multiple TestSheets, watch for Attribute structures that will show up again elsewhere, and convert them into Classes (Lesson 6) rather than rebuilding them each time. A Class can then be amended — immediately or as the project evolves — to include new data variations, and every TestSheet referencing it benefits.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The recommended core structure
entries.text: Keep using the four-Attribute skeleton from Lesson 2 as the backbone of every TestSheet: Administration (BusinessRelevant = No), Precondition and Process (BusinessRelevant = Yes), and Verification (BusinessRelevant = Result). Populate each with the relevant sub-Attributes and Instances for that Requirement.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Structuring for Agile: Given-When-Then

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Given-When-Then
entries.text: A template for writing acceptance tests for user stories, useful when TestCase Design needs to reflect an Agile way of working. An acceptance test built this way has three parts: Given (the context and preconditions), When (the action being carried out), Then (the observable, expected outcome).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Worked example
entries.text: User story: 'As a returning customer, I want my saved shipping address pre-filled at checkout, so I can complete an order faster.' Written as Given-When-Then: Given a registered customer with a saved shipping address is logged in, When they proceed to checkout, Then the saved address should be pre-filled and the customer should be able to confirm the order without re-entering it.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Building structure outside Tosca first

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why plan externally
entries.text: For a large or complex TestSheet, it can be faster to sketch the Attribute hierarchy in Notepad or Excel first, then import it in one shot, instead of creating each Attribute by hand inside Tosca.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Readability & maintainability guidelines

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Hands-on

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 10 - Automatic Generation of Instances
entries.text: Lesson 10 - Automatic Generation of Instances (video)

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Automating what you've done manually

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The goal
entries.text: TestCase Design exists to generate complete test data sets from the Attributes and Instances you've defined. Everything built manually so far — combining at a lower Attribute level or at the TestSheet level using Linear Expansion — can instead be generated automatically by Tosca in one action.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: How it works
entries.text: Focus on the level where you want combinations created, and Tosca instantly combines every structural element beneath that level according to the combinatorial method you select.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Generating at a lower Attribute level

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Prerequisite: an empty Instance Folder
entries.text: To generate Instances automatically on a specific Attribute, that Attribute first needs an empty Instance Folder — because the lower Attributes being combined will automatically combine into the next Instance Folder above them. Create this by adding an Instance (which creates both the Instance itself and its containing Instance Folder), then deleting just the Instance while keeping the Folder.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Generating
entries.text: With the Instance Folder in place, select the Attributes to combine, right-click, choose 'Generate Instances', and pick the combinatorial method. The combinations appear as Instance columns according to that method.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Generating at the TestSheet level

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Simpler — no Folder setup needed
entries.text: At the TestSheet level, there's no need to pre-create an Instance Folder. Just right-click the TestSheet itself, select Generate Instances, and choose the method. Any combinations already created at lower levels are automatically taken into account when Tosca generates at the TestSheet level.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Generate Instances vs Complete Instances

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The problem with re-generating after a change
entries.text: If a new Attribute is added later and 'Generate Instances' is run again, Tosca does not account for the combinations that already existed — it can recombine everything and potentially create duplicates.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Complete Instances
entries.text: The fix: 'Complete Instances' only creates the new combinations required to cover the newly added Attribute, leaving existing combinations untouched and un-duplicated. It works the same way as Generate Instances — available at both the TestSheet and Attribute level, via right-click → Complete Instances → choose method.

entries.title: About this module

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Capstone review
entries.text: The official course closes with three unguided scenarios where you design a TestSheet from a business description alone, without step-by-step instructions: a discount-calculation feature, a configurable-product feature, and an abstract billing-package feature. Each is meant to force you to apply Lessons 1-10 end to end, without being told which Attribute or method to use. This module walks through one original worked example the same way, then reviews what each official scenario is really testing conceptually.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Worked example: a Loyalty Tier discount

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Business context
entries.text: A webshop is introducing a Loyalty Tier discount at checkout: Guest checkouts (no loyalty account) get no discount, Bronze members get 5% off the subtotal, Silver members get 10% off, and Gold members get 15% off. An expired loyalty account should be rejected with an error at checkout rather than receiving any discount.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Step 1 — Requirement
entries.text: Under Folder 'Webshop' → RequirementSet 'Checkout', create a Requirement 'Apply loyalty discount'. Since pricing-related bugs have high financial impact but this feature isn't used on every order, it's reasonable to weight it with Complex Weighting — a mid Frequency Class and a higher Damage Class.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Step 2 — Attributes
entries.text: Create a TestSheet 'Loyalty Discount at Checkout' with the four core Attributes: Administration (No), Precondition (Yes — e.g. an active customer session), Process (Yes — the Loyalty Tier itself), Verification (Result — the expected discount applied).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Step 3 — Instances
entries.text: Under the Process Attribute's 'Loyalty Tier' Attribute, create Instances: Guest (StraightThrough — the most common, lowest-dependency case), Bronze (Valid), Silver (Valid), Gold (Valid), and Expired Account (Invalid — expected to produce a rejection error, not a discount).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Step 4 — Combinatorial method
entries.text: With one Attribute driving four meaningfully different behaviors, Linear Expansion is the natural fit here: the Guest StraightThrough becomes the baseline TestCase, and each remaining Instance (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Expired Account) becomes its own TestCase differing only in Loyalty Tier — giving 5 TestCases total, each with an isolated, easy-to-debug focus. All Combinations would be unnecessary here since there's only one Attribute actually varying.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Step 5 — Reuse and linking
entries.text: If 'Loyalty Tier' is likely to be reused in other TestSheets (e.g. a separate Requirement for loyalty point accrual), it's a good candidate to extract into a Class once that second use case appears — not before. Finally, all 5 generated Instances get dragged onto the 'Apply loyalty discount' Requirement, creating TestCase-Substitute links that make this coverage visible on the Requirements dashboard.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: Where TDS fits in Tricentis Test Data Management

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: Test Data Management (TDM)
entries.text: The umbrella term for Tricentis' holistic data solution, made up of several components: Test Data Service, TDM Studio, qTest, and Flood.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: TestCase Design vs. Test Data Service

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: Recap: TestCase Design (TDS1)
entries.text: TestCase Design structures TestCases to cover every variant and pathway of the SUT, producing the combinations needed for comprehensive coverage. Static data values can be added, but this data is non-consumable — it can be reused multiple times and simultaneously by different TestCases.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: Test Data Service (TDS2)
entries.text: TDS acts as a data repository where records can be stored, retrieved, updated, and have their status viewed by multiple people. Unlike TestCase Design's static data, TDS stores consumable/dynamic data that regularly changes — this data can generally only be used once, by one machine, at a time.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: Test data, defined
entries.text: Any information fed into the application under test — usernames, passwords, credit card numbers, customer details, reference data, and more.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: Two core challenges TDS solves

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: Challenge 1 — Acquiring specific test data
entries.text: Complex database structures often require specific data that isn't available in the SUT or is hard to access. A direct SQL query would normally retrieve it, but suitable SQL statements are often missing, or slow and difficult to write. Existing data (production data, or data created in an earlier test) is another option, but retrieving it manually is time-consuming. TDS solves this either way: it can generate the needed test data on demand, or store and adjust already-available data — both with fast response and run times.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: Challenge 2 — Tracking the state of test data
entries.text: An earlier test frequently changes the data it touched. If inaccurate, old, or already-consumed data gets reused by another TestCase, results become unreliable — a risk that grows sharply when end-to-end TestCases span several days or run on multiple machines.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: Worked example — why state matters
entries.text: Two TestCases logging into the same SAP account to modify personal details can't run at the same time; the second must wait for the first to finish and then use the updated values. A more complex case — creating a bank customer, generating an account number, then processing a payment — needs each dynamic value (customer ID, account number) progressively updated in the TDS repository as it's produced, or a later step (like processing the payment) simply won't have a valid ID to work with.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.title: How TDS keeps data stateful
entries.text: TDS gives visibility into a multi-tester environment by adjusting each record's Status as it moves through the process, and prevents conflicting use of the same record through lock/unlock features. Data can also be created, retrieved, or updated through API calls, which further increases response time and agility when managing test data.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Theory Lesson - Introduction to Test Data Service
entries.title: Test Data Service (TDS)
entries.text: A server-based application with a web-based portal that displays test data in a table-like structure. This web page is called the Test Data Management page, or the Test Data Object Viewer, and can be reached from any browser by typing the right endpoint request.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Theory Lesson - Introduction to Test Data Service
entries.title: How Tosca Commander and TDS talk to each other

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Theory Lesson - Introduction to Test Data Service
entries.title: The connection
entries.text: Before any of this works, a connection must be established between Tosca Commander and Test Data Service through installation and configuration (covered in Lesson 1). Once set up, TestCases in Tosca are built to specify what should happen to the test data — the common functions being create, find, update, and delete. TDS Standard Modules exist specifically to perform these functions quickly.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Theory Lesson - Introduction to Test Data Service
entries.title: The request/response flow
entries.text: When a TestCase runs, Tosca Commander instructs the SUT what to do, and simultaneously exchanges a series of endpoint requests with TDS — creating, finding, updating, or deleting records as needed. Every change is reflected back in the TDS repository's table-like view.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Theory Lesson - Introduction to Test Data Service
entries.title: Worked example: profile → file → upload
entries.text: A 3-step process — create a user profile, create a file, upload the file — becomes 3 separate TestCases: (1) create a new user account, which shows up as a new entry in the TDS repository; (2) find/retrieve that account's data from TDS, log into the website with it, and create the file — the record is then updated to a new state in TDS; (3) retrieve the newly created file's data and use it to upload the file — the record is updated again to reflect that.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Theory Lesson - Introduction to Test Data Service
entries.title: An analogy for the three roles
entries.text: Tosca works like the project Manager, sending requests for what needs to be done. TDS plays two roles: the Reporter, giving a clear overview of project status, and the Document Controller, storing all the relevant documents (test records) under the right categories (types).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Theory Lesson - Introduction to Test Data Service
entries.title: This course's scenario: the DemoWebShop order process

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Theory Lesson - Introduction to Test Data Service
entries.title: How the repository evolves through the process
entries.text: 1) Adding an address moves a customer's Status from New to Active. 2) Adding items to the cart populates an 'items' column with the count. 3) Purchasing items creates an OrderNumber column and sets OrderStatus to Pending. 4) The payment is processed through non-UI commands, moving the backend status from Pending to Processing. 5) That change is then reflected in the TDS repository's OrderStatus field, Pending → Processing. 6) Once the order is fully completed, its Test Records are moved into a new TDS type called 'Used'.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 2 - Create and Register records through TDS
entries.title: Where the module lives
entries.text: TDS Standard Modules are found under Standard Modules → Test Data Management → Test Data Service. To register a new record, add a TestStep and insert the module 'Test Data - Create & provide new record', which writes new entries into the TDS repository's table-like structure.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 2 - Create and Register records through TDS
entries.title: Using the module
entries.text: Expand the module's Data structure Attribute and fill in every required Attribute and value — this is exactly what gets stored under the TDS type you select. The TestStepValue 'Existing or new TDS type*' lets you pick an existing type or create a brand-new one on the fly.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 2 - Create and Register records through TDS
entries.title: Alias name

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 2 - Create and Register records through TDS
entries.title: What it's for
entries.text: Alias name is an optional field that labels a specific record within a dataset. If left blank, the TDS type itself is used as the alias — e.g. the TDS type 'CustomerDetails' becomes the record's alias by default.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 2 - Create and Register records through TDS
entries.title: When it actually matters
entries.text: Alias name exists to distinguish between different roles that share the same TDS type. For example, a customer could be either the sender or the recipient in a bank transaction — two roles with different tasks in the SUT that need to be tested separately. Without a distinct alias, both would be grouped under the same TDS type, and a TestCase could fail by testing a sender's flow when a recipient's data was actually needed.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 2 - Create and Register records through TDS
entries.title: Quick self-check
entries.text: True or False: (1) If Alias name is left blank, it takes the name of the 'Existing Attribute' — FALSE, it actually takes the name of the TDS type, not any Attribute. (2) Alias name must be used when you have different record types performing different functions in the SUT — TRUE.

entries.text: On the Test Data Management page, the landing page shows every configured repository as a tile. Opening one reveals a Types column on the left (types created via Standard Modules appear in blue, each with a small green badge showing its record count). Selecting a type displays all of its records, table-like, on the right.

entries.title: Worked example: registering a DemoWebShop customer

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 2 - Create and Register records through TDS
entries.title: Inputs and initial state
entries.text: First name, last name, and email — already captured as Buffers from the registration TestCase — are fed into 'Create & provide new record' as its inputs. The Status Attribute is set to 'New', which flags freshly registered customers so they can be retrieved later specifically in that state. OrderNumber and OrderStatus are left blank at this point — they get filled in progressively as the customer moves through later steps (purchase, payment, etc).

entries.title: Repetitions
entries.text: To generate several test records in one go, set a Repetitions value on the relevant Execution Entry. From the Ribbon's Context Menu, choose Repetition, enter the desired count in the 'Replace with' field, and select 'Modify All'. A value of 5, for example, produces 5 test records. The same setting can also be changed directly in the Properties pane for that Execution Entry.

entries.title: TestData - Find & provide record
entries.text: Retrieves a previously created record via a search query. The 'Existing TDS type*' field defines which dataset to search (e.g. CustomerDetails).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: ActionMode Constraint
entries.text: Restricts the search to records matching a specific condition — e.g. TDS attribute Status = 'New', to find only newly registered customers rather than any customer record.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)

entries.title: Entering retrieved data: the {TD[...]} expression

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: Syntax
entries.text: Once a record is found, its values are fed into the SUT using the {TD[...]} expression, entered directly in a TestStepValue's Value field — the same style of expression used elsewhere in the Automation Specialist courses. The part right after the opening brace is the command to retrieve a test record from the TDS repository; the part in square brackets identifies exactly which value, as TDSType.AttributeName.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: Worked example
entries.text: To log a newly registered customer into the DemoWebShop using their retrieved email address, the Value field would contain: {TD[CustomerDetails.Email]} — retrieve a record from the CustomerDetails type and use its Email attribute.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: Updating a test record

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: TestData - Update record
entries.text: Used whenever a record's data needs to change — e.g. once a newly registered customer adds an address, their Status should move from New to Active. Updating a record in TDS always works together with a search: you must first find the correct record, then apply the update to it.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: Matching the search identity
entries.text: The TestStepValue 'Existing alias name (record)*' on the Update module must match the value used earlier when the record was searched for — in this example, 'CustomerDetails'. The update itself targets a TDS attribute (Status) and supplies its new value (Active, replacing New).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: How the repository evolves through the order process

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: Payment processing — a two-step update
entries.text: Step 1 (backend): non-UI Standard Modules search for a record with OrderStatus = Pending, then send non-UI requests carrying that OrderID plus the customer's email and password to the backend. Tosca verifies a 200 OK response, confirming the payment succeeded — this moves the status to Processing in the backend system itself, but NOT yet in TDS. Step 2 (repository sync): Tosca searches again for that same Pending-OrderStatus record, verifies the DemoWebShop now shows it as Processing, and only then updates the TDS repository's copy of that record to Processing.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: Moving consumed records to a new TDS type

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: Why move data at all
entries.text: Once the full order process (including payment) has run, that customer's data is considered consumed. Moving it into a distinct TDS type keeps the repository stateful — it's immediately clear which records are still 'live' and which have already been used, which is especially valuable for a distributed team.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 3 - Retrieving and Updating Test records through TDS
entries.title: TestData - Move record to TDS type
entries.text: Searches for records under the existing TDS type (e.g. CustomerDetails) and relocates them to a new type under a new name (e.g. CustomerDetails_Used). The TestStepValue 'Existing alias name (record)*' takes the CURRENT type's value (CustomerDetails), while 'Existing or new TDS type*' takes the DESTINATION type's value (CustomerDetails_Used).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - Introduction to the Standard TestData - Expert Module
entries.title: TestData - Expert Module
entries.text: Rather than assembling a TestCase from several separate Standard Modules (Create, Find, Update...), the Expert Module performs all of those functions itself, plus extra ones the standalone modules don't offer — ReadOnly, deleting individual records, and deleting entire types. It's included in the Standard.tsu subset, under Standard modules → Test Data Management → Test Data Service.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - Introduction to the Standard TestData - Expert Module
entries.title: Test data task*
entries.text: The Expert Module's key TestStepValue is a dropdown listing every supported function: Create, ReadOnly, Find, Update, DeleteType, DeleteRecord, DeleteAll. Whichever is selected tells Tosca exactly what to do with the data in that TestStep.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - Introduction to the Standard TestData - Expert Module
entries.title: The seven Test data task options

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - Introduction to the Standard TestData - Expert Module
entries.title: ReadOnly: the one function that doesn't lock

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - Introduction to the Standard TestData - Expert Module
entries.title: What makes it different
entries.text: Every other Test data task locks the record it touches by default. ReadOnly is the exception: it reads the data without modifying it, and explicitly does NOT lock the record — leaving it free for others to use.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - Introduction to the Standard TestData - Expert Module
entries.title: When to reach for it
entries.text: ReadOnly fits data meant to be reused across many TestCases at once — contract data, user ID numbers, reference data, or credit card numbers. For example, a bank transaction test might just need 'any' valid Visa card number, with no requirement that it be unique to that test. In a distributed environment, several testers on different workspaces need to be able to borrow that same reference record simultaneously.
